text:
Maya: Seeing streaming token jitter from us-west2 gpupool-5 — several customer streams hit gRPC deadlines and we have big spikes in packet reordering counters on those hosts. Dashboard: https://console/redwood/streams?range=15m :rotating_light:
Liam: I pulled traces — deadlines line up with reorder spikes. Captured tcpdump on gpu-node-5a around 18:22. Snippet:
--- tcpdump ---
16:22:17.123456 IP src=10.2.5.12 dst=10.2.5.33 len 1400 (retransmission)
16:22:17.123789 IP src=10.2.5.33 dst=10.2.5.12 len 60
(reordering counts incrementing)
--- end ---
Sophia: quick check: ethtool shows host NIC MTU=9000 but ToR/leaf is 1500. RDMA sessions fall back and we see interleaved large/short frames -> reordering. ethtool -k ens1f0:
rx-checksumming: on
gro: on
tso: on
rx-vlan-offload: on
Devon: ethtool -S gives high rx_nohandler and rx_fifo_errors on the affected NICs. rdma_cm logs show: "ib_device: CQ overflow, STag invalid" intermittently. Likely jumbo mismatch + rx coalescing causing out-of-order delivery for streaming tokens.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-007 / priority P2 — channel #inc-INC-2026-007 created. Pager: @Oliver assigned.
Oliver: Oncall ack. Watching traces and SLOs. Set an alert for >0.3% gRPC deadline rate.
Maya: Short term mitigation proposal: disable GRO/TSO and lower rx-usecs on affected NICs, and canary traffic shift off the rack. Commands we can run on one node:
for NIC in $(ls /sys/class/net | grep ens); do
  ethtool -K $NIC gro off tso off
  ethtool -C $NIC rx-usecs 30 rx-frames 8
done
Also cordon the node before draining heavy streaming pods: kubectl cordon gpu-node-5a && kubectl drain gpu-node-5a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
Liam: Iperf3 tests between host and ToR show reorder when using 9k -> 1500 translation: iperf3 -c 10.2.5.1 -l 64k
[  5]  0.00-10.00  sec  1.12 GBytes  962 Mbits/sec  0.20% packet_reorder
Also saw RDMA pingpong show unexpected STag errors when MTU mismatch.
Sophia: Longer term: either standardize MTU 9000 across fabric (hard) or enforce 1500 at host level. Option 2 is lower risk and faster. We'll coordinate with network team to avoid breaking other workloads.
Devon: I'll run the canary on rack gpupool-5 (3 nodes) starting in 10m. Plan: 1) cordon node, 2) apply ethtool changes, 3) run perf tests and tail logs for reorder counters, 4) uncordon. Script: https://infra-scripts/repro/disable_offloads.sh (internal)
Maya: Sounds good. Can we also temporarily bump streaming fallback window and increase gRPC deadline by +100ms for affected route to reduce customer impact while we test? Patch is trivial in routing config.
Liam: I can push the routing tweak as a short-lived canary with 10% traffic shift to fallback model. Will monitor token latency and error rate.
Oliver: I'll keep a close eye on tracing and SLOs. If gRPC deadline errors >0.5% or reorder counters start increasing again after change, roll back immediately.
Maya: Assigning tasks: Devon -> run canary + script; Liam -> route tweak + monitor; Oliver -> oncall + rollback authority; Sophia -> coordinate with network team re: MTU policy.
Devon: Starting canary in ~8m on gpu-node-5a. Will post logs here.
Maya: Thanks. Keep messages short — post exact ethtool/iperf outputs and a final verdict when done.
Liam: Noted.
Oliver: ack.
